evidence: The hunk shows `methods: RpcMethod[]` still listing "detach" with `toBe(14)` after detach left RpcRequest; 34b031e drops it and asserts 13. The agent also correctly diagnosed why CI missed it (root tsconfig references only src/).
guidance_note: When removing a union variant, grep the whole repo for its literal (tests and docs included) before pushing, since tsc --build does not read the test files here.

evidence: IMPL.md still said "Fire methods (currently only `detach`)" after detach was removed; 34b031e applied the suggested wording. The same fix left identical stale wording in rpc-dispatch.ts, which round 1 flagged as F7 and F9.
guidance_note: When fixing a stale phrase, grep for the phrase ("fire methods") across code comments as well as docs and fix every hit in the same commit.

evidence: The comment/code mismatch is real: the hunk shows `listener(_event, ...args)` under a comment saying the wrapper strips the event. The agent fixed the comment and kept the code, arguing renderer.ts:84 expects `(_event, ...args)`. The packet does not include renderer.ts, so whether dropping the event would really break the bridge cannot be checked here.
guidance_note: Write the comment explaining why a wrapper exists from the code as it is now, and state the real reason (stable identity for removeListener), not one remembered from an earlier draft.

evidence: The original Badge had an onClick but no component prop, even though its own comment named the `component="button"` escape hatch. 34b031e adds component="button", type="button", aria-label and disabled.
guidance_note: When a comment names the technique the code needs (component="button"), make the code use it before pushing; a comment describing intended code that is not there is a review finding waiting to happen.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the hard-coded `tmux kill-session -t xterm-electron-demo` on the default server is in the original spec, and 34b031e touched only IMPL.md, App.tsx, wrapper-tracker.ts and connectors-rpc.test.ts. The premise holds, and 61a7742 isolates the tests on a per-run `-L` socket with kill-server.
guidance_note: Tests that spawn tmux should start on an isolated `-L` socket from day one, as the repo's integration tests already do; never target a fixed name on the user's default server.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the `const SESSION = "xterm-electron-demo"` on the default server in main.ts predates 34b031e, which did not touch main.ts. The fix threads `-L <socket>` with env overrides through every call.
guidance_note: Same move as F5: give a demo that shells out to tmux its own `-L` server, configurable by env, when it is first written.

evidence: F2's fix (34b031e) rewrote the IMPL.md "fire methods synthesize their own CommandResponse" sentence but left the same clause in rpc-dispatch.ts's header ("fire methods synthesize their own CommandResponse so the caller never has to know"). Round 1 flagged that remainder.
guidance_note: When a reviewer flags a stale claim in a doc, grep the codebase for the same claim; the doc paragraph mirrored a code comment that needed the same edit.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: engine.ts was not touched by 34b031e, so this is original keymap logic. Pressing the prefix twice in prefix mode fell into the unbound-chord row and was swallowed, unlike tmux's default C-b C-b send-prefix. The fix adds a table row and tests binding priority.
guidance_note: When a keymap engine imitates tmux, list tmux's default prefix-table behaviours (send-prefix included) as test cases before writing the outcome table.

evidence: The dispatchRpcRequest docstring still said "fire methods synthesize their own success response" while every DISPATCH entry returns a CommandResponse. It is the second leftover copy of the claim F2's IMPL.md fix removed.
guidance_note: Same move as F7: one grep for the stale phrase during the F2 fix would have caught both code copies.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: e2e.spec.ts's fixed-name kill-session on the default server is original code that 34b031e did not touch. It is the same issue as F5, and 61a7742 fixed both together.
guidance_note: Same move as F5: isolate every tmux-spawning test on its own `-L` socket when writing it.

narrative: Round 0 raised four valid points: a stale detach test, a stale doc, a wrong comment and a11y. The agent fixed them in 34b031e and correctly pushed back on the reviewer's suggested code change for F3. Round 1 found two leftover copies of the stale 'fire methods' claim the F2 fix should have swept (F7, F9), plus four issues in original code the reviewer had not reached in round 0: tmux session isolation and send-prefix. Round 1 would have happened anyway for those, so no round was avoidable, but two of its findings were.
guidance_observations: The agent noticed tests were outside the tsc project graph but only suggested it as a follow-up; wiring them in during the PR would have turned this class of finding into a CI failure.
For a doc-staleness finding, the agent fixed the cited location rather than the claim everywhere it appeared.

evidence: The hunk shows the comment "client.close to release the pending FIFO entry" above code that calls only handle.dispose(). The agent trimmed the comment and also removed a dead `void t` the reviewer missed.
guidance_note: Before pushing, reread each cleanup comment against the lines under it; a comment drafted while still deciding on an approach describes code that was never written.

narrative: There was a single round with one comment-accuracy finding, accepted and fixed in 91cd307. It caused no follow-on findings.
guidance_observations: The only finding was a comment describing code that was never written; reading comments against code as a self-review step would have avoided the round.

evidence: The hunk shows both the `close` and `error` listeners running `closeCallbacks.forEach`, and a WebSocket error is followed by close, so onClose fired twice. 209d83f routes both through a single guarded dispatcher and adds an error-then-close test.
guidance_note: When adapting an event source to a single-shot callback such as onClose, list which source events can fire in sequence (error then close) and give them one guarded dispatch point from the start.

evidence: `atob` throws on malformed input, and decodeBase64 ran it unguarded inside the message handler. The agent took the reviewer's emitError/in-error option and correctly rejected the empty-bytes substitution as a silent fallback.
guidance_note: Treat every decode of peer-supplied data (atob, JSON.parse) as a trust-boundary parse and give it an explicit error path when first written.

narrative: One round with two valid robustness findings in new adapter code, both accepted. On F2 the agent picked the explicit-error option and rejected the empty-bytes fallback.
guidance_observations: Both findings were in input-handling paths of new transport code; listing the failure inputs for each boundary handler before writing it would have covered both.

evidence: The hunk shows `execSync(`tmux -L ${socket} has-session -t ${session}`)` with the socket now chosen through renderer IPC, which is a real shell-injection path. a5da471 routes the calls through one argv helper.
guidance_note: When a value newly arrives from IPC or the renderer, convert every shell-string use of it to argv in the same change; grep execSync across the repo, tests included.

evidence: pickSessionOn interpolated the picker-supplied socket into an execSync template string. It is the same injection class as F1, fixed in the same commit.
guidance_note: Same move as F1: one grep for execSync template strings covers every instance.

evidence: The doc says "minus `default` and the currently-attached socket", and the agent confirms the implementation includes default. The doc was updated to match the intended contract. The reply-hint 'pushback' is lexical; the agent accepted.
guidance_note: Write the interface doc for a cross-process API by reading the handler that implements it, not from the plan.

evidence: The config comment claims a "PID-aliveness check", but the reviewer and agent agree that global-setup only runs `tmux -L NAME list-sessions` and unlinks dead sockets. The comment was reworded.
guidance_note: Don't describe a safety guarantee in a comment unless the code implementing it is in the diff.

evidence: The hunk shows the exported isTmuxServerAlive running `execSync(`tmux -L ${socketName} list-sessions`)` on a public input. It was switched to execFileSync argv.
guidance_note: Public library functions that spawn processes should take argv from the first commit; a library export has no trusted callers.

narrative: One round with five valid findings: three shell-interpolation sites and two inaccurate comments, all accepted in a5da471. The argv sweep covered main.ts and sockets.ts but not the e2e specs in the same PR, which still used execSync templates; #9 later flagged four of those (F1-F4).
guidance_observations: The execSync-to-argv fix was applied to the sites the reviewer named, not to every execSync in the PR's own files; the e2e specs carried the same pattern into #9's review.

evidence: The agent confirms `this.abort` is never read or passed to any listener, so the controller gated nothing. It was removed and the teardown docs were rewritten to describe the real dispose path.
guidance_note: Don't add a teardown mechanism (AbortController) without wiring its signal into at least one consumer in the same change; delete it otherwise.

evidence: The constructor assigns stallLow/High from options without checking the documented `low < high` invariant. 099272a validates once at construction and tests the invalid cases.
guidance_note: When a doc comment states an invariant between options ("Must be < stallHighChunks"), enforce it in the constructor in the same commit that writes the comment.

evidence: The hunk shows `bridge.onEvent(...)` with its unsubscribe discarded, inside a helper called per mount, which contradicts the "never grows" comment. The fix attaches lazily and detaches when the last handler goes.
guidance_note: Every subscribe call's returned unsubscribe must be stored and reachable from a dispose path; check this for each `on`/`onEvent` call before pushing.

evidence: The hunk resets only when `prev` is closed or connecting. Whether WebSocketBridge really passes through `open` before `ready` depends on code the packet does not show, though the agent confirmed it. The reset-on-next-ready latch is correct either way, so accepting was right.
guidance_note: When detecting a lifecycle transition, key on 'has left the ready state since the last ready' rather than on the immediately previous state, which ties the logic to one assumed state order.

narrative: One round with four findings: dead teardown machinery, an unenforced documented invariant, a leaked bridge listener and a fragile reconnect check. All were accepted in 099272a. The leaked-listener pattern recurred in the library version of the same adapter in #7 (F4), written in parallel.
guidance_observations: Three of the four findings are code whose comments promise something the code doesn't do (gating, an invariant, "never grows"); checking each such comment against the code would have caught them before review.

evidence: The hunk shows the fake `okResponse` with `command`, `output: ""` and `error` fields, which don't match CommandResponse; this compiles only because tests are outside tsc's graph (see #1/F1). The fake was rewritten to the real shape.
guidance_note: Build test fakes from the real type, for example with a typed factory, and get the test files into the typechecked project so shape drift fails CI.

evidence: The mount() JSDoc still referred to container dimensions after the ResizeObserver was deleted; the agent confirmed the stale wording was still present despite the outdated flag. The JSDoc was updated.
guidance_note: When deleting a mechanism (ResizeObserver), grep the file's comments for what it did ("container") and update them in the same commit.

evidence: The hunk shows `client.execute(`switch-client -t ${session}`)` unquoted, right after an ensureSession call that does quote. The fix uses the canonical tmuxEscape for both and removes the duplicate quoter.
guidance_note: When writing a tmux command string next to a helper that already quotes, use the same quoter; mixing quoted and unquoted forms of one argument is the gap.

evidence: paneSessionClientFromBridge discards the bridge.onEvent unsubscribe, the same leak as #6/F3. Both PRs were opened at the same time and #6's fix landed after this code was written, so it is not caused by a fix. The lazy attach/detach fix has tests.
guidance_note: When promoting demo code into the library, carry over the fixes being made to the demo copy in parallel PRs, or extract it from one source so the fix lands once.

narrative: One round with four valid findings, all accepted in 2549bce. F4 repeats #6/F3's listener leak in the promoted library adapter. The two PRs were stacked and reviewed simultaneously, so the duplicate was a parallel-copy problem, not a fix regression.
guidance_observations: Running parallel PRs over copies of the same adapter meant one defect was reviewed and fixed twice.

evidence: The hunk shows `"command": "npx", "args": ["electric-cherry"]` without -y, unlike the neighbouring entry. The fix adds -y and pins @0.1.1.
guidance_note: When adding a config entry, copy the conventions of the existing sibling entry (npx -y, a pinned version).

evidence: cherry-chrome-mcp used `pnpm dlx` in a repo whose other entry uses npx and which has a package-lock. It was switched to `npx -y`.
guidance_note: Use the repo's existing package runner in new tooling config instead of the one from the author's machine.

evidence: The hunk shows `github:brandon-fryslie/cherry-chrome-mcp` as a floating ref. The agent pinned it to commit e228994 after confirming there was no npm package or tag.
guidance_note: Pin any github: dependency to a commit when adding it.

narrative: A small config PR with one round and three valid reproducibility findings, all fixed in one commit (3860991). It caused no follow-on findings.
guidance_observations: All three findings were departures from the neighbouring config entry's conventions.

evidence: The e2e specs still used `execSync(`tmux -L ${name} kill-server`)` after #5's argv sweep (a5da471) converted only main.ts and sockets.ts, though both specs were in #5's file list. The real reason for the fix is avoiding shell parsing; a per-spec copy of the `tmux()` helper is not a single enforcer.
guidance_note: When converting execSync-with-interpolation to argv for one finding, grep every execSync in the repo (tests and specs included) and convert them all in the same commit.

evidence: killAltSockets runs `execSync(`tmux -L ${name} kill-server`)`, another site #5's argv sweep skipped. Fixed in f761efb with the shared spec helper.
guidance_note: Same move as F1: sweep the pattern across the repo, not just the reported line.

evidence: The alt-socket bring-up runs `execSync(`tmux -L ${ALT_SOCKET} new-session ...`)`, the same unswept pattern. It was converted to the argv helper.
guidance_note: Same move as F1.

evidence: killSocket in web-multiplexer-dom.spec.ts uses the execSync template string. It was fixed with a second copy of the helper in that spec.
guidance_note: Put the argv tmux helper in one shared test module rather than copying it into each spec.

evidence: swapTo disposes the bridge and nulls `active` before connecting, so a dead target strands the app. The agent took the reviewer's pre-flight isTmuxServerAlive suggestion and reasoned the rollback away, since createMainBridge cannot coexist with the old handlers and a rollback is itself a fallible connect. That split answer is defensible.
guidance_note: When writing a teardown-then-rebuild swap, validate the target before the first destructive step.

evidence: The hunk adds `ourSockets.add(socket)` after any new-session, including on an already-running user server, so quit could kill-server the user's tmux. 162d49b probes liveness first and excludes `default`. The cited law is decoration: the fix is still an `if` inside a catch.
guidance_note: Record ownership of a shared resource at the point the resource itself is created (the server), not at a side effect that can also happen on someone else's resource (a session).

evidence: The hunk shows `catch { return false; }`, so ENOENT (no tmux) reads as a dead server and the prune would unlink sockets. The catch-all already existed in the execSync version before #5's argv change, so this is not fix-caused. 5b4391d treats only a numeric `status` as dead.
guidance_note: A probe's catch should only map the specific failure it expects to `false` and rethrow the rest; write the error-shape check when writing the probe.

evidence: disposeApp in the original DOM spec awaits app.close() then killSocket, so a rejected close leaks the socket. This code predates every review fix; round 1 ran on the same head commit 9698e76. Wrapped in try/finally in 499d931.
guidance_note: Put resource cleanup in try/finally (or afterEach) whenever an earlier awaited step can throw.

evidence: This duplicates F6, raised in round 1 against the same original commit 9698e76 on code already rewritten in 162d49b. The agent correctly replied already_fixed with the commit.

narrative: This is the re-landed socket-picker work from #5. Round 0 found four execSync interpolation sites in e2e specs that #5's argv sweep skipped, plus three real ownership and error-handling bugs; all were fixed sensibly, and F5 got a reasoned partial answer. Round 1 ran against the same original head commit, so its two findings (one new, one duplicate of F6) are not fix-caused.
guidance_observations: Four of the nine findings were the leftover of a sweep from an earlier PR; a repo-wide grep at the time of #5's fix would have closed them.
The fix copied the argv helper into each spec instead of sharing one module, which reintroduces the duplication the cited single-enforcer law is meant to prevent.

evidence: BridgeProtocolError was imported but unused. The agent took the reviewer's alternative ("assert on the error type explicitly"), which also tightened the tests from message regex to type assertion.
guidance_note: Run the linter before pushing; an unused import is a lint error the agent could have seen locally.

evidence: BridgeError was imported but unused, while the test docstring promised BridgeError(TIMEOUT). The agent asserted instanceof plus code, the reviewer's second option, and the test now matches its docstring.
guidance_note: When a test docstring names an error type, assert that type rather than matching message text.

evidence: The JSDoc claims an "exhaustive check below" but none exists, and `satisfies readonly TmuxMessage["type"][]` only checks membership, not completeness. The fix derives the Set from a `satisfies Record<SerializedEventType, true>` map, which gives real exhaustiveness.
guidance_note: When a comment claims compile-time exhaustiveness, use a Record-keyed map; an array `satisfies` check only proves membership.

evidence: The hunk shows `const known = new Set(["vertical", "target"])` built on every validation call; it was hoisted to module scope. It is a minor, correct cleanup.

narrative: Round 0 raised four small valid findings: two unused imports, a false exhaustiveness claim and a per-call allocation. All were fixed in 836d26b, and round 1 found nothing. For the unused imports the agent chose the stronger option of asserting on the error types.
guidance_observations: Two of the four findings were lint errors that a local lint run before pushing would have caught.
